evidence.requirements: Most of the brief is met. Start page has the heading, Search and Family controls, the count text and exact-name links (app.js:43-68, list.jpg). Detail facts, tables grouped by section with Symbol/Value/Unit, Print button, 'All cartridges' link and hash routes are in place (app.js:107-142). Tolerances sit inline with their value (format.js:99-117). Angles show as 40° or 10°58'00" (format.js:62-67). The SVG has the name '<name> drawing', a hatched section, a dash-dot centre line, the required dimensions and a title block. Partly met: (1) on screen the title block says 'Scale fit to width' instead of a scale; a real scale only appears in print (drawing.js:494-496). (2) The printed drawing is not at full width: it fills about 40% of the A4 width at 'Scale 0.93 : 1' (print-308_win.jpg, style.css:363-367). (3) Belted solid-head depth w adds E+tb as well as ramp end+tb (geometry.js:410-411), so 300 Win. Mag. gets w=6.19 where the brief's rule gives 4.8. (4) The spec/process artefacts are missing: openspec/specs holds only .gitkeep.
evidence.correctness: The geometry follows the rules closely. Rim classification is at geometry.js:56-75. Chamfer uses min(f·tanβ, R1/4) (:131-134). The rimfire half-round has radius min(R/2,(R1-P1)/2) (:123-128). Groove, floor and ramp are at :148-171, and the belt ramp at δ to the axis is at :160. The shoulder runs through published points with r1 min and r2 fillets (:190-195). The tangent ogive radius formula is at :259-266, the quarter ellipse at :246-256, and seating depth and k by shape and category at :224-243. The heeled bullet uses H2 and H2-2tb (:388-389). Walls tn and tb are at :369-370, the shoulder blend is linear (:286-291), and pocket sizes are at :12-13. The screenshots match the references in outline and proportions: 308 shoulder and neck, the 300 WM belt, the 9 mm taper with round nose, the 22 LR heeled bullet with half-round rim, the 44 Mag semi-wadcutter cone, and the 9,3x74 R shallow 10°58' shoulder. Values match the data, and print is one A4 page (print test plus print-308_win.jpg). Deviations: belted w as noted above, and the print scale shows the drawing below true size.
evidence.security: All data is escaped before innerHTML (escapeHtml at app.js:11-17, used throughout), and SVG text goes through escapeXml (drawing.js:24-30). There is no eval or Function. The e2e test asserts that only file:// requests are made (app.test.js:29-37). The data URLs appear only as links.
evidence.code_quality: Small IIFE modules with clear names and responsibilities: data, format, catalogue, geometry, drawing, app. Missing values are reported, not invented (geometry.js:144-147, 186-189), and unknown keys get a not-found view (app.js:96-103). Minor issues: escapeHtml and escapeXml are duplicated; format.capacityText is unused by the app; the .not-found CSS rule is unused; and drawing.js layout() is a dense collision engine with modest commenting.
evidence.tests: node:test unit suites cover rim types, the chamfer, the rimfire half-round, groove and belt ramp end, the shoulder angle, seating and k, the ogive tangent and meplat, heeled bullets, walls and w, primer pockets, missing-value handling, label overlaps and the outline, mandatory dimensions, tolerance formatting and the title block. Playwright e2e covers file:// with no requests, search with alternative names, the family filter, reload persistence, tables without Tol rows, print hiding, the footer, one-page PDF for 4 cartridges, a 360 px phone width, dark mode and a static server. Gaps: no flat or semi-wadcutter nose tests, the inner wall line is only loosely checked, there is no belted w check, and print legibility or full width is not tested.
evidence.ux_design: The tables are dense, right-aligned and use tabular numbers, which suits engineers (detail-308_win.jpg). The drawing panel works poorly. Fixed 3 mm label text makes the labels dominate the small cartridges: 22 LR and 9 mm labels are about 30 px, larger than the page h1 (detail-22_long_rifle.jpg, detail-9_mm_luger.jpg). The staircase leaves a large empty band above the part. The title block is oversized (name about 40 px) with a meaningless 'Scale fit to width'. The print layout is tidy with a 4-column table grid, but the drawing is small and centred. Table headers in print are larger than the cell text.
evidence.accessibility: The SVG has role=img and aria-label '<name> drawing' (drawing.js:355). Inputs are wrapped in labels (app.js:45-48). Table headers use th scope=col, the count is aria-live, the page is lang=en, and buttons and links are native. Muted text #5d6671 on white passes contrast. Gaps: no figcaption or long description for the drawing, no focus management on route change (only scrollTo), and default focus styles only.
evidence.simplicity: No runtime dependencies and one dev dependency (playwright pinned). About 1,350 lines of plain JS and CSS across six files, appropriate for the geometry and layout work. There is a little dead code: capacityText, .not-found, and the duplicated escape helpers.
evidence.maintainability: package.json has test scripts, pinned playwright 1.64.1 and a lockfile. However there is no README, no CI configuration, no docs, ADRs or specs (openspec/specs/.gitkeep is empty), and no engines field or .nvmrc for Node 22. The `npx playwright install` step for the e2e tests is undocumented. Code comments explain the rules, and the regression tests are good.
evidence.visual_design: The start page is calm and clean (list.jpg). Detail pages mix tiny UI text (facts at about 12 px, table headers) with oversized SVG text (labels and title block), so the typography is inconsistent. The blue dimensioning on white looks tidy and drafting-like, and the outlines are crisp. Print is consistently black on white.
evidence.layout: The order is right: name, facts, drawing, tables. Inside the drawing frame, though, the part occupies a thin band. In detail-308_win.jpg the figure is about 700 px tall for a part about 60 px tall, with large label stairs and an empty title-block area. The two-column table grid leaves large holes beside short groups. There are no overlaps or clipping in any screenshot. The print page leaves about 15% blank at the bottom while the drawing stays small.
evidence.usability: Navigation is simple: list link, detail, 'All cartridges' back, bookmarkable #/cartridge/<key>, and back/forward work (tested). Search is live and matches alternative names. Print is one click. The not-found view gives a way back. The list has no sorting options and no per-row family filtering beyond the select, but the brief's tasks take few steps.
evidence.reception: Reloaders and engineers would trust the data tables and the correctly proportioned, rule-based drawings. However, the oversized labels and title block, plus 'Scale fit to width', look less polished than OpenBallistics. The small printed drawing undercuts the print use case. They would probably use it, with reservations.

unmet_requirements: Title block on screen shows 'Scale fit to width' instead of a scale (drawing.js:494-496); a real scale appears only in print
Printed drawing is not at full width: about 40% of the A4 width at 0.93:1 (print-308_win.jpg, style.css:363-367)
Belted solid-head depth w also uses E+tb, against the brief's 'or the belt ramp end + tb on belted cases' (geometry.js:410-411)
Process artefacts (specs, docs) not delivered: openspec/specs is empty
strengths: Geometry follows the brief's rules faithfully (chamfer, rimfire half-round, groove, belt ramp at δ, shoulder fillets, ogive, ellipse and cone noses, heeled bullet, walls and primer pockets), and outlines match the reference proportions
Strong automated checks: label-overlap and outline-collision tests over all 25 records, mandatory-dimension checks, a one-page A4 PDF test, file:// with no network requests, and phone width
Secure, dependency-free plain JS with consistent escaping, correct value, tolerance and angle formatting, and complete grouped tables
issues: Drawing presentation: fixed 3 mm label text and an oversized title block dwarf the part, leave large empty areas, and give the screen view a non-scale 'Scale fit to width'
Print drawing is far from full width (about 40% of the A4 width, below true size), wasting the page the brief wanted the drawing to fill
No README, CI, docs, ADRs or runtime pinning: a new developer has nothing but the code and tests
review.verdict: The engineering core is solid: the geometry follows the brief's rules, the data is shown correctly, and the tests are unusually thorough, including label collisions and one-page print. The drawing's visual scaling (oversized labels and title block, no real on-screen scale, small print drawing) and the missing project documentation and CI need work before publishing.
